Jakarta's old town is full of history, as it was formally the capital of the Dutch East Indies. Known as Batavia, it was a well fortified European style town and many of the old colonial buildings still stand today.

After enjoying a local snack, that I thought was going to be more of a drink, called Es Selendang Mayang, I took a horse ride around the old city. It was a nice, relaxing way to explore a bit while getting shade from the scorching sun.

I then visited a very fancy restaurant called Jajaghu that had very reasonable prices. I enjoyed their Nasi Tumpeng, which is a cone-shaped serving of rice with sides of vegetables and meat originating and is a traditional Javanese food.

The restaurant had load of dessert options but I felt like going for more of a wander around the old town and finding something sweet from the street
title: Exploring Jakarta's Oldest Neighbourhood (400 Year Old Dutch Batavia) 🇮🇩

author: Dale Philip
description: I visited Kota Tua, the old town of Jakarta and was looking to enjoy a horse ride there. I couldn't find the horses but one friendly local man offered me a ride on his friend's back.
title: Human Horse Ride in Jakarta, Indonesia 🇮🇩

author: Dale Philip
description: I visited Kota Tua, the old town of Jakarta, where I found this vendor selling an interesting iced dessert / drink called Es Selendang Mayang. It's a traditional Betawi food so it's very popular with local people in Jakarta.
title: Trying 'Selendang Mayang' in Jakarta, Indonesia 🇮🇩
